rationale: Cadence is a developer-infrastructure startup. The direction is high-contrast and instrument-like: a near-black canvas, a single electric accent, and monospace detailing so the product feels engineered rather than marketed. Type stays geometric and tight; the accent is rationed so it always signals action or state, never decoration.

palette.semantic: Graphite — the dominant dark surface; app chrome and hero backgrounds.
Raised panel — cards and elevated surfaces one step above the base.
Electric blue — the single action color; buttons, links, active states, and focus rings.
Void — the base canvas behind everything.
Off-white — primary body text at high contrast on dark surfaces.
Slate grey — secondary labels, metadata, and inactive controls.

typography.semantic: A geometric grotesque with mechanical detailing — reads engineered and modern for product headlines.
A neutral workhorse for documentation-dense body copy; excellent at small sizes on dark backgrounds.
Monospace for code, metrics, and status readouts — carries the engineered feel into the details.

layout.semantic: A single centered headline over a subtle grid, letting the product claim breathe before any UI is shown.
Three equal columns for capability cards — even weighting signals a platform, not a single feature.

cohesion.summary: Extremely cohesive: one accent, one dark family, and monospace as the only textural variation. The restraint reads as engineering discipline.

principles.title: Ration the accent
principles.detail: Electric blue only ever means an action or an active state — never a background, divider, or decoration.

principles.title: Monospace is signal, not style
principles.detail: Reserve the mono face for data, code, and status; using it for prose dilutes what it communicates.

principles.title: Contrast over color
principles.detail: Hierarchy comes from surface elevation and text contrast, not from adding hues — the palette stays near-monochrome on purpose.
